prompt: Stage 2-1, prismatic augment, 100 HP, level 4 with 9 gold. Your opener is four random 1-costs with no shared trait; you have not scouted yet. Options: Delayed Payout (8 gold at the start of every stage from now on), Trait Crown (emblem, 2-star unit and an item for a named trait) and Radiant Promise (one item turns radiant at 5-1). Which do you take?
explanation:
Prismatic expectations are the point: a prismatic should decide the game, and the question is which of these decides it in your favour given what you know. At 2-1 you know nothing: no scout, no direction, four unrelated 1-costs. The Crown is enormous power, but it locks you into a vertical before you have seen whether three other players opened it, and a contested Crown at 3-2 is a board that cannot hit its own units. Delayed Payout at 2-1 with 100 HP is the safe prismatic: 8 gold at 3-1, 4-1, 5-1, 6-1 is 32 gold plus the interest it compounds, roughly a full extra rolldown, and it leaves you free to take whichever line the 3-2 scout shows is open. The prismatic ceiling is preserved because the gold is spent on 4-costs at the moment you know which ones.

Radiant Promise is the worst of the three here: it does nothing for four stages and you have no item worth making radiant yet. Note the reversal from the low-HP case: at 100 HP with the whole game ahead, an econ prismatic is a ceiling-raiser; at 40 HP on 4-2 the same augment would be a trap.
principle: Prismatic augments should decide the game; at 2-1 with no information, take the one that decides it later, when you know more.
commonMistake: Taking the Crown for the raw power and discovering at 3-2 that two players opened the same trait.
